fields.Name: ORD-26 - Capture Payment
fields.Description: Orders.CapturePayment, the operation the UI was blocked on (CP1-CP12). A payment is a header plus its allocation lines written in ONE transaction, and PaymentHeaderEntityServer.Lines is a TRANSIENT collection rather than a column - CodeGen cannot emit it client-side, so a browser entity.Save() had nowhere to put the allocations and taking a payment in the UI was impossible rather than merely unwired. The checks are weighted toward the decisions where a plausible choice is wrong: over-payment must be ACCEPTED and become spendable credit rather than refused, because the account-credit screen depends on negative balances existing; idempotency must return the ORIGINAL payment rather than a second one or a spurious error; and Preview must run the real capture and roll it back rather than modelling the arithmetic separately, because a separate model eventually disagrees and the disagreement is a balanced journal entry for the wrong amount.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: A capture writes the header and its allocation lines together in one transaction; the tender resolves by CODE and an unknown code is refused by name rather than defaulting; the order rollups move and the output reports the same figures read back rather than recomputed; the capture books balanced journal entries so the ledger and the order cannot disagree; an allocation total that does not equal the amount is refused with the shortfall named rather than silently adjusted; a payment splits across two orders and closes both; over-payment is accepted, leaves a negative balance and is flagged as credit; an order belonging to another company is refused by name; a repeated IdempotencyKey returns the original payment with WasRetry set and moves money once; a different key on the same shape takes a second legitimate payment; Preview returns the real numbers and leaves no row behind; and injected or malformed ids are refused at the boundary rather than reaching filter text.
